# Aim:
Here we want to investigate if the transposon insert determines hopping efficiency. 
To do so we have different options. First we want to plot the hopping efficiency of all constructs from LP-116kb in the Sox2 locus, to establish the notion that the insert matters to hopping from the same LP. 
Then use TF reporters, same location (N1), different activities. Would expect a negative correlation between activity and hopping efficiency. 
Do the same comparisons for NanogS and NanogL in the same locus. 
Compare Sox2P in WT vs DelE vs DelE vs mCh_del (need to think if we can use mCh_del for this)


## TF reporter inserts
pLD01 - NanogP_S with SV40 polyA in right direction, otherwise insert is same as in pCM008


## NOTE
E2866 has been sorted for GFP- cells after the barcoding, therefore we do not use it in this analysis. 
We only use E2828.

## Curate dataset - remove bad samples
Notes: there seems to be something wrong with the fw mapping of E1792_N31_D11_fw, E1792_N37_D4_fw, E1792_N37_D11_fw (very few reads and basically no home reads). I filter for samples that have sufficient reads:
```{r}
#check how many samples have low total reads
hopping_eff_tib %>% filter(total_reads < 500) %>% pull(sample_name)
hopping_eff_tib %>% filter(home_reads < 100) %>% pull(sample_name)

#How different are the Tdgf1 samples
hopping_eff_tib %>% filter(grepl("Tdgf1", sample_name))

#Set filter so that Tdgf1 is included but the bad home location samples are not
hopping_eff_tib_filt_2 = hopping_eff_tib %>%
  dplyr::filter(home_reads >= 15)
```
Filtering this way removes most of the Tdgf1 samples, apparently they are sequenced very shallow. 
The fract_home reads of the samples is between 22-36% and it looks like the fraction is increasing with later timepoints of harvested gDNA. This could indicate that there is still hopping going on, specially between D4 and D8. 


## Annotate tibble
Caution with the following samples:
**E2866**: Cells were sorted for GFP-, so they are biased not just for barcoded cells but also for hopped integrations to a silent location, so not really fair to use them. 
**E2143**: These cells are a mix of pCM008 and pCM10, do not use therefore. 
```{r}
hopping_eff_tib_wide = hopping_eff_tib_filt_2 %>%
  mutate(sample_base = str_remove(sample_name, "_(Fw|Rv|fw|rv)$")) %>%
  select(-sample, -sample_name, -total_reads, -home_reads) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(sample_base, launch_pad), names_from = orientation, values_from = fract_home_reads) %>%
   rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
         fw_over_rv = fw/rv, #to detect problematic samples
         mean_fract_home = mean(c_across(cols = c(fw,rv)), na.rm = T), #(fw+rv)/2,
         mean_fract_hopped = 1-mean_fract_home,) %>%
  filter(!grepl("E2143", sample_base)) %>% #filter out E2143 & E2866
  #filter(!grepl("E2866", sample_base)) %>% 
  ungroup()


hopping_eff_tib_wide_grouped = hopping_eff_tib_wide %>%
  mutate(sample_group = case_when(sample_base %in% paste0("E2288_MVP", 1:5) ~ "E2288_MVP_C1",
                                  sample_base %in% paste0("E2288_MVP", 6:10) ~ "E2288_MVP_C6",
                                  sample_base %in% paste0("E2048_NanogS08_P", 31:39) ~ "E2048_NanogS08",
                                  sample_base %in% paste0("E2048_NanogS10_P", 1:51) ~ "E2048_NanogS10",
                                  grepl("E2226|E2285|E2292", sample_base) ~ str_remove(sample_base, "_[0-9]*$"),
                                  .default = sample_base)) %>%
  group_by(launch_pad, sample_group) %>%
  mutate(launch_pad = case_when(grepl("Fzd5", sample_base) ~ "Fzd5", 
                                grepl("Tdgf1", sample_base) ~ "Tdgf1",
                                .default = launch_pad)) %>%
  summarize(mean_fw = mean(fw),
            mean_rv = mean(rv),
            mean_fract_home  = mean(mean_fract_home),
            mean_fract_hopped  = mean(mean_fract_hopped ))


# write_tsv(hopping_eff_tib_wide_grouped, "CM20250819_summary_hopping_efficiency.tsv")
```

## annotate dataframe
Infos to constructs:
CM002 and CM003 have a short PA signal (snRP1)
CM008 has SV40 polyA signal, wrong orientation (same as Sox2 constructs)
CM010 has short polyA signal (snRP1)

pCM002 is short Nanog promoter
pCM003 is long Nanog promoter
pCM008 is short Nanog promoter
pCM010 is short Nanog promoter

pCM002, pCM008, pCM010 have the same short Nanog promoter sequence
```{r}
# In the pipeline, the nested PB-SB pLD037 inserts are given the same launch pad position, called N1 in this case. This is because they all have the same sequence because they are not reaching the genome, therefore we have to assign the right LP here. 


samples_annotated = hopping_eff_tib_wide %>%
  mutate(sample_group = case_when(sample_base %in% paste0("E2288_MVP", 1:5) ~ "E2288_MVP_C1",
                                  sample_base %in% paste0("E2288_MVP", 6:10) ~ "E2288_MVP_C6",
                                  sample_base %in% paste0("E2048_NanogS08_P", 31:39) ~ "E2048_NanogS08",
                                  sample_base %in% paste0("E2048_NanogS10_P", 1:51) ~ "E2048_NanogS10",
                                  grepl("E2226|E2285|E2292|E2143", sample_base) ~ str_remove(sample_base, "_[0-9]*$"),
                                  .default = sample_base)) %>%
  select(sample_base, sample_group, launch_pad) %>%
  mutate(experiment = str_remove(sample_base, "_.*$"),
         insert = case_when(experiment == "E1177" ~ "pJOYC037",
                            experiment %in% c('E1682', 'E1792') ~ 'pLD037',
                            experiment == "E1665" ~  "pME013", #cell line CBS16 = pME013
                            grepl("NanogS08", sample_base) ~ "pCM008",
                            grepl("NanogS10", sample_base) ~ "pCM010",
                            experiment == "E2288" ~ "pMV001",
                            experiment == "E2143" ~ NA, #check, I think this is actually a mix of pCM008 and pCM010, so cannot really analyse
                            grepl("16A", sample_base) ~ "pME016",
                            grepl("CBS16", sample_base) ~ "pME013",
                            grepl("_34", sample_base) ~ "pME034",
                            grepl("_41", sample_base) ~ "pME041",
                            grepl("3xCTCF", sample_base) ~  "pME038",
                            grepl("CRE6", sample_base) ~ "CRE6",
                            grepl("MK[0]?1", sample_base) ~ "pMK01", #matches MK01 and MK1
                            grepl("MK[0]?2", sample_base) ~ "pMK02",
                            grepl("MK[0]?3", sample_base) ~ "pMK03",
                            grepl("MK[0]?3", sample_base) ~ "pMK03",
                            experiment == "E2902" ~ "pJOYC037",
                            grepl("_LoxP", sample_base) ~ "pLD037",
                            sample_base == "E1845_NanogS" ~ "pCM002",
                            sample_base == "E1845_NanogS_techrep1" ~ "pCM002",
                            sample_base == "E1845_NanogL" ~ "pCM003",
                            sample_base == "E1845_NanogL_techrep1" ~ "pCM003",
                            grepl("NRF1", sample_base) ~ "TFR_NRF1",
                            grepl("OCT4SOX2", sample_base) ~ "TFR_Oct4_Sox2",
                            grepl("P53", sample_base) ~ "TFR_P53",
                            grepl("E2866_Nanog", sample_base) ~ "pLE001",
                            grepl("Random2", sample_base) ~ "TFR_neg_ctrl",
                            grepl("STAT3", sample_base) ~ "TFR_STAT3"),
         launch_pad = case_when(grepl("Fzd5", sample_base) ~ "Fzd5", 
                                grepl("Tdgf1", sample_base) ~ "Tdgf1",
                                .default = launch_pad)
  )

sample_group_annotated = samples_annotated %>%
  dplyr::select(-sample_base) %>%
  distinct()

```

# Transposition efficiency based on transposon cargo
Combine insert pME013 and pME016 together. 
Also combine pCM02, pCM08, pcM010 and use the mean hopping efficiency and mean size
I am using the different NanogS as different biological replicates since they have the same NanogS promoter and only differ in their polyA. 

```{r Transposition efficiency for differnt cargo categories}
insert_cat_levels <- c(
  "neutral_1", "neutral_2", "CTCF", "promoter", "synthetic_promoter",
  "CTCF+promoter", "gene", "enhancer", "other"
)

plot_dat2 =
hopping_eff_tib_wide_annot2 %>% 
  select(launch_pad, insert, insert_category, bio_rep, mean_fract_hopped, genotype, experiment) %>% 
  filter(launch_pad %in% c("LP23", "N1", "C9"),
         genotype == "WT",
         experiment != "E2866") %>%
  mutate(insert_plot = case_when(insert == "pME016" ~ "1xCBS",
                                 insert %in% c("pCM002", "pCM008", "pCM010") ~ "NanogS",
                                 insert == "pME034" ~ "Sox2P",
                                 insert == "pME041" ~ "Sox2P_CDS",
                                 insert == "CRE6" ~ "neutral_2",
                                 insert == "pLD037" ~ "neutral_1",
                                 insert == "pME013" ~ "1xCBS",
                                 insert == "pME038" ~ "3xCBS",
                                 insert == "pMK01" ~ "3xCBS_Fw_Sox2P",
                                 insert == "pMK02" ~ "3xCBS_Rv_Sox2P",
                                 insert == "pMK03" ~ "1xCBS_Fw_Sox2P",
                                 insert == "pCM003" ~ "NanogL",
                                 insert == "pMV001" ~ "Nanog Enhancer",
                                 .default = insert))  %>%
  mutate(insert_plot = factor(insert_plot, 
                              levels = (c("neutral_1", "neutral_2", "1xCBS", "3xCBS", "1xCBS_Fw_Sox2P", "3xCBS_Fw_Sox2P", "3xCBS_Rv_Sox2P", "Sox2P", "Sox2P_CDS", "NanogL", "NanogS", "TFR_neg_ctrl", "TFR_P53", "TFR_STAT3", "TFR_Oct4_Sox2", "TFR_NRF1", "Nanog Enhancer")))) %>% #order them for plotting
 mutate(bio_rep = case_when(insert == "pCM002" ~ "rep1", #use the different NanogP cargos as different reps
                             insert == "pCM008" ~ "rep2",
                             insert == "pCM010" ~ "rep3",
                             .default = bio_rep)) %>%
  mutate(insert_category = factor(insert_category, levels = insert_cat_levels)) %>%
  group_by(launch_pad, insert_plot, bio_rep, insert_category) %>% 
  summarize(mean_fract_hopped_biorep = mean(mean_fract_hopped), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(insert_lp = paste(launch_pad, insert_plot, sep = "_"))
  
```
**Conclusion:**
Here 1xCBS consists of pME013 and pME016 combined. NanogS contains pCM02, pCM08, pcM010, same NanogS promoter but different polyA. Used each one as a separate biologcial replicate. Describe in M&M. 

## Fig 3A  plot
```{r Fig 3A}
summary_stats = plot_dat2 %>% 
  group_by(insert_plot, launch_pad, insert_category) %>%
  summarise(mean_fract_hopped = mean(mean_fract_hopped_biorep)) %>% ungroup()

pHopEff_LP_inserts_V2 =
  plot_dat2 %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = insert_plot, y = mean_fract_hopped_biorep,
             col = insert_category)) +
  #geom_jitter(alpha = 0.8, size = 2, width = 0.2) +
  #geom_jitter(alpha = 0.8, size = 2, width = 0.2, height = 0) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
  geom_point(data = summary_stats, aes(x = insert_plot, y = mean_fract_hopped), 
             shape = "-",
             size = 10,
             color = "black") +
  facet_nested(~ launch_pad, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_x_discrete(
    drop = TRUE,
    labels = function(x) sub(".*__", "", x)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.7)) +
  ggtitle("Transposition efficiency for different inserts",
          subtitle = "E2866 filtered out") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  scale_color_manual(values = insert_category_cols)

pHopEff_LP_inserts_V2
```

## Fig 3B - Insert size of chosen LPs
Same filtering as before:
- here we take the mean of the biologcial replicates
- and we take the mean of the size of the NanogS constructs, the only difference here is the polyA tail, the promoter is the same. Insert size ranges from 1485 to 1671 bp. 
```{r Fig 3B}

  filter(launch_pad %in% c("LP23", "N1", "C9"),
         genotype == "WT",
         experiment != "E2866") %>%
  mutate(insert_plot = case_when(insert == "pME016" ~ "1xCBS",
                                 insert %in% c("pCM002", "pCM008", "pCM010") ~ "NanogS",
                                 insert == "pME034" ~ "Sox2P",
                                 insert == "pME041" ~ "Sox2P_CDS",
                                 insert == "CRE6" ~ "neutral_2",
                                 insert == "pLD037" ~ "neutral_1",
                                 insert == "pME013" ~ "1xCBS",
                                 insert == "pME038" ~ "3xCBS",
                                 insert == "pMK01" ~ "3xCBS_Fw_Sox2P",
                                 insert == "pMK02" ~ "3xCBS_Rv_Sox2P",
                                 insert == "pMK03" ~ "1xCBS_Fw_Sox2P",
                                 insert == "pCM003" ~ "NanogL",
                                 insert == "pMV001" ~ "Nanog Enhancer",
                                 .default = insert))  %>%
  mutate(insert_plot = factor(insert_plot, 
                              levels = (c("neutral_1", "neutral_2", "1xCBS", "3xCBS", "1xCBS_Fw_Sox2P", "3xCBS_Fw_Sox2P", "3xCBS_Rv_Sox2P", "Sox2P", "Sox2P_CDS", "NanogL", "NanogS", "TFR_neg_ctrl", "TFR_P53", "TFR_STAT3", "TFR_Oct4_Sox2", "TFR_NRF1", "Nanog Enhancer")))) %>% #order them for plotting
 mutate(bio_rep = case_when(insert == "pCM002" ~ "rep1", #use the different NanogP cargos as different reps
                             insert == "pCM008" ~ "rep2",
                             insert == "pCM010" ~ "rep3",
                             .default = bio_rep)) %>%
  mutate(insert_category = factor(insert_category, levels = insert_cat_levels)) %>%
  group_by(launch_pad, insert_plot, bio_rep, insert_category, insert_size) %>%
  summarize(mean_fract_hopped_biorep = mean(mean_fract_hopped), .groups = "drop") %>% #calculate mean per bio_rep from tech_reps
  group_by(launch_pad, insert_plot, insert_category) %>% # combine per insert construct
  summarize(mean_fract_hopped = mean(mean_fract_hopped_biorep),
            mean_insert_size = mean(insert_size),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(insert_lp = paste(launch_pad, insert_plot, sep = "_"))


ggplot(plot_dat3, 
       aes(x = mean_insert_size, y = mean_fract_hopped, color = insert_category, shape = launch_pad)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(group = 1),
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "black") +
  stat_cor(
    data = plot_dat3,
    aes(x = mean_insert_size, y = mean_fract_hopped),
    method = "spearman",
    inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.7)) +
  ggtitle("Hopping efficiency vs insert size", subtitle = "N1, LP23, C9 LPs, Spearman corr.") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_manual(values = insert_category_cols) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

```

## Normalize expression
```{r}

#subtract autofluorescence, normalize to GFP
autofluo_tib_comb = fcs_tib  %>%
  filter(name == "WT") %>%
  summarize(mCherry_WT = mean(median_mCherry),
            GFP_WT = mean(median_GFP) )

mCherry_WT <- autofluo_tib_comb$mCherry_WT
GFP_WT     <- autofluo_tib_comb$GFP_WT

expression_tib_comb = fcs_tib %>%
  mutate(median_mCherry_cor = median_mCherry - mCherry_WT,
         median_GFP_cor     = median_GFP - GFP_WT,
         GFP_norm           = median_GFP_cor / median_mCherry_cor)


#normalize to random 2 control (the mean of both replicates)
standard_tib = expression_tib_comb %>%
  filter(insert == "random2") %>%
  summarize(mCherry_standard = mean(median_mCherry_cor),
            GFP_standard = mean(median_GFP_cor) )

mCherry_standard <- standard_tib$mCherry_standard
GFP_standard <- standard_tib$GFP_standard

expression_tib_comb = expression_tib_comb %>%
  mutate(rel_mCherry_cor = median_mCherry_cor / mCherry_standard,
         rel_GFP_cor = median_GFP_cor / GFP_standard)
```

## Add hopping efficiency to it
```{r}

# Filter for E2828 & E2866

tib_comb %>%
```

```{r}
#add sample names and phenodata
```

## Statistics 
```{r}
# Calculate median expression
tib_median = as_tibble(rownames = "name", fsApply(flowset_fluo, each_col, median)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(median_GFP = GFP,
         median_mCh = mCherry,
         median_mTurq = mTurq) %>%
  select(-c("FSC", "SSC"))

# Calculate mean expression
tib_mean = as_tibble(rownames = "name", fsApply(flowset_fluo, each_col, mean)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(mean_mCh = mCherry,
         mean_GFP = GFP,
         mean_mTurq = mTurq) %>%
  select(-c("FSC", "SSC"))

# Calculate standard deviation
tib_std = as_tibble(rownames = "name", fsApply(flowset_fluo, each_col, sd)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(std_mCh = mCherry,
         std_GFP = GFP,
         std_mTurq = mTurq) %>%
  select(-c("FSC", "SSC"))
  
tib_mean_median_std = tib_median %>% 
  left_join(tib_mean, by = "name") %>%
  left_join(tib_std, by = "name") %>%
  mutate(CV_mCh = std_mCh/mean_mCh, 
         CV_GFP = std_GFP/mean_GFP,
         CV_mTurq = std_mTurq/mean_mTurq)

tib_all = pheno_data_tib %>% left_join(tib_mean_median_std, by = "name")

#To add cell number
tib_all = tib_all %>% left_join(fcs_files_combined)
```

## Correct and normalize medians
```{r}
#subtract autofluorescence
autofluo_tib_comb = tib_all  %>%
  filter(cell_line == "WT") %>% #WT rep1 has low amount of cells recorded
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarize(mTurq_WT = mean(median_mTurq),
           mCherry_WT = mean(median_mCh),
            GFP_WT = mean(median_GFP) )

#normalize to GFP
expression_tib_comb = tib_all %>%
  left_join(autofluo_tib_comb, join_by(date)) %>%
  mutate(median_mTurq_cor = median_mTurq - mTurq_WT,
         median_mCherry_cor = median_mCh - mCherry_WT,
         median_GFP_cor = median_GFP - GFP_WT) %>%
  mutate(mTurq_norm = median_mTurq_cor / median_GFP_cor,
         mCherry_norm = median_mCherry_cor / median_GFP_cor)

#normalize to 23_34A (to compare between measurement days and to compare them in general)
standard_tib = expression_tib_comb %>%
  group_by(date, experiment) %>%
  filter(cell_line == "23_34A" & treatment == "untreated") %>%
  summarize(mTurq_norm_standard = mean(mTurq_norm),
            mCherry_norm_standard = mean(mCherry_norm),
            GFP_standard = mean(median_GFP_cor))

expression_tib_comb = expression_tib_comb %>%
  left_join(standard_tib, join_by(date, experiment)) %>%
  mutate(rel_mTurq = mTurq_norm / mTurq_norm_standard,
         rel_mCherry = mCherry_norm / mCherry_norm_standard,
         rel_GFP_cor = median_GFP_cor / GFP_standard)
```

## Correlate hopping efficiency with activity
E2270 (hopping) and E2282 (mapping) are the exp for rep1
E2239 (hopping) and E2347 (mapping) are the exp for rep2
```{r}

# hopping efficiency
tib_hop_eff_delD_delE = hopping_eff_tib_wide_annot2 %>% 
  filter(experiment %in% c("E2282", "E2347") & insert == "pME034") %>%
  mutate(cell_line = case_when(genotype == "delD2" ~ "23_34_D2",
                               genotype == "delE12" ~ "23_34_E12",
                               genotype == "WT" ~ "23_34A",
                               .default = genotype)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(replicate = bio_rep) %>%
  select(mean_fract_hopped, mean_fract_home, cell_line, replicate, insert, insert_size, GC_content)

tib_try = expression_tib_comb %>% left_join(tib_hop_eff_delD_delE, join_by(cell_line, replicate))
```

### Fig S4B Final paper plot
We have hopping from two biological replicates and one FACS measurment per clone. 
```{r Fig S4B}
# Hopping efficiency of each individual replicate
tib_hop_eff_delD_delE_allRep = 
hopping_eff_tib_wide_annot2 %>% 
  filter(insert == "pME034" & launch_pad == "LP23") %>%
  mutate(cell_line = case_when(genotype == "WT" ~ "23_34A",
                               genotype == "delD2" ~ "23_34_D2",
                               genotype == "delE12" ~ "23_34_E12"))

# rel_mTurq level of rep2
tib_rel_mTurq_rep2 =  expression_tib_comb %>% 
  filter(treatment == "untreated" & replicate == "rep2") %>% 
  select(cell_line, rel_mTurq, mTurq_norm)

# mean of hopping efficiency
tib_summary = tib_hop_eff_delD_delE_allRep %>% 
  group_by(genotype) %>%
  summarise(mean_fract_hopped = mean(mean_fract_hopped)) %>% 
  mutate(cell_line = case_when(genotype == "WT" ~ "23_34A",
                               genotype == "delD2" ~ "23_34_D2",
                               genotype == "delE12" ~ "23_34_E12"))

tib_summary_V2 = tib_summary %>% left_join(tib_rel_mTurq_rep2, join_by(cell_line))


#combine to one tibble for plotting
tib_comb_DelD_DelE = tib_hop_eff_delD_delE_allRep %>% 
  left_join(tib_rel_mTurq_rep2, join_by(cell_line))

# Plot
pDelD_DelE_cor_rep2 = 
tib_comb_DelD_DelE %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = rel_mTurq, y = mean_fract_hopped, col = cell_line)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2.5) +
  geom_crossbar(
    data = tib_summary_V2,
      aes(x = rel_mTurq, y = mean_fract_hopped, ymin = mean_fract_hopped, ymax = mean_fract_hopped, col = cell_line),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    width = 0.1,
    alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  ggtitle("Hop eff. of Sox2P in LP23 for diff. genomic background", subtitle = "rel mTurq expression based on rep2") +
  theme_bw()

pDelD_DelE_cor_rep2
```

### Normalize expression
```{r}
#subtract autofluorescence
autofluo_tib_comb = fcs_tib_all  %>%
  filter(filenames %in% c("WT_neg_ctrl_rep1", "rep2_WT_neg_ctrl_rep2_001", "round1_WT_ctrl_005", "round2_WT_ctrl_005")) %>% 
  group_by(bio_rep) %>%
  summarize(mTurq_WT = mean(median_mTurq),
            mCherry_WT = mean(median_mCherry),
            GFP_WT = mean(median_GFP))

#normalize to GFP
expression_tib_comb = fcs_tib_all %>%
  left_join(autofluo_tib_comb, join_by(bio_rep)) %>%
  mutate(median_mTurq_cor = median_mTurq - mTurq_WT,
         median_mCherry_cor = median_mCherry - mCherry_WT,
         median_GFP_cor = median_GFP - GFP_WT) %>%
  mutate(mTurq_norm = median_mTurq_cor / median_GFP_cor,
         mCherry_norm = median_mCherry_cor / median_GFP_cor)

#normalize to 23_34A (to compare between measurement days and to compare them in general)
standard_tib = expression_tib_comb %>%
  filter(launch_pad == "LP23" & genotype == "WT") %>%
  group_by(bio_rep) %>%
  summarize(mTurq_norm_standard = mean(mTurq_norm),
            mCherry_norm_standard = mean(mCherry_norm),
            GFP_standard = mean(median_GFP_cor))

expression_tib_comb = expression_tib_comb %>%
  left_join(standard_tib, join_by(bio_rep)) %>%
  mutate(rel_mTurq = mTurq_norm / mTurq_norm_standard,
         rel_mCherry = mCherry_norm / mCherry_norm_standard,
         rel_GFP_cor = median_GFP_cor / GFP_standard)
```

# Figure S4A - Nanog long vs short E1845
In E1891 we tested Nanog long (pCM003) vs Nanog small (pCM002) promoter
almost same activity but different size. 
```{r}
hopping_eff_tib_wide_annot2 %>% filter(experiment == "E1845" & insert %in% c("pCM002", "pCM003")) %>%
  mutate(merge_name = paste0(experiment, "_", launch_pad, "_", insert))

```

## Load FACS data
```{r}
#Load FCS files
fcs_files_E1891 = dir("/home/c.moene/projects/hopping_technology/04_Hopping_eff_insert_activity/FACS_files/E1845_E1891", full.names = T)
names(fcs_files_E1891) = str_remove(str_remove(str_remove(fcs_files_E1891, '.*/'), "_Single Cells.fcs"), "export_")


annotation_file_E1891 = tibble(filenames = names(fcs_files_E1891),
                               full_filename = fcs_files_E1891,
                               insert_name = case_when(grepl("S4", filenames) ~ "NanogS",
                                                  grepl("L1", filenames) ~ "NanogL",
                                                  .default = "control"),
                               insert = case_when(grepl("S4", filenames) ~ "pCM002",
                                                  grepl("L1", filenames) ~ "pCM003",
                                                  .default = "control"),
                               launch_pad = "N1",
                               genotype = "WT", 
                               bio_rep = "rep1",
                               experiment = "E1845",
                               merge_name = paste0(experiment, "_", launch_pad, "_", insert))
   
# Load FCS files
flowset_E1891 = flowCore::read.flowSet(files = annotation_file_E1891$full_filename, alter.names = T, truncate_max_range = F, ignore.text.offset = T)

#make dataframe
annotation_file_E1891 = data.frame(annotation_file_E1891)
rownames(annotation_file_E1891) = annotation_file_E1891$filenames

flowCore::sampleNames(flowset_E1891) = annotation_file_E1891$filenames
flowCore::pData(flowset_E1891) = annotation_file_E1891

flowset_fluo_E1891 = flowset_E1891[,c('BL1.A')]
colnames(flowset_fluo_E1891) = c("GFP")
```

```{r}
total_cell_count_tmp = flowCore::keyword(flowset_fluo_E1891, "$TOT")[,'$TOT']
total_cell_count = as.numeric(total_cell_count_tmp)
names(total_cell_count) = names(total_cell_count_tmp)


median_GFP = sapply(1:length(flowset_fluo_E1891), function(i){
  median(flowCore::exprs(flowset_fluo_E1891[[i]])[,'GFP'])
})
names(median_GFP) = sampleNames(flowset_fluo_E1891)

flowCore::pData(flowset_fluo_E1891)$median_GFP = median_GFP
flowCore::pData(flowset_fluo_E1891)$total_cell_count = total_cell_count

fcs_tib_E1891 = tibble(flowCore::pData(flowset_fluo_E1891))
```

## autofluo corrected
```{r}
tib_E1891_autofluo = 
fcs_tib_E1891 %>% filter(insert == "control") %>%
  select(median_GFP) %>%
  dplyr::rename(median_GFP_ctrl = median_GFP)

fcs_tib_E1891 = fcs_tib_E1891 %>% bind_cols(tib_E1891_autofluo) %>%
  mutate(GFP_cor = median_GFP - median_GFP_ctrl) 

fcs_tib_E1891_sel = fcs_tib_E1891 %>% 
  select(insert_name, insert, launch_pad, merge_name, GFP_cor, total_cell_count)

```

## Normalize
```{r}
# Normalize NanogL to NanogS
E1891_NanogS_GFP_cor = fcs_tib_E1891_sel %>% filter(insert_name == "NanogS") %>% select(GFP_cor) %>% dplyr::rename(GFP_cor_NanogS = "GFP_cor")

fcs_tib_E1891_sel = fcs_tib_E1891_sel %>% 
  bind_cols(E1891_NanogS_GFP_cor) %>%
  mutate(rel_GFP = GFP_cor/GFP_cor_NanogS)
```
**Conclusion:** 
NanogL is 1.29 higher than NanogS expression. 


## Plot
```{r}
tib_hop_eff_E1891 =
hopping_eff_tib_wide_annot2 %>% filter(experiment == "E1845" & insert %in% c("pCM002", "pCM003")) %>%
  mutate(merge_name = paste0(experiment, "_", launch_pad, "_", insert)) %>%
  left_join(fcs_tib_E1891_sel)

```

### Plot hopping efficiency as barplot
```{r}
#Define Nanog colors
nanog_cols <- c(
  "control" = "grey75",
  "NanogS" = "#4DB6AC",
  "NanogL" = "#E69F00"
)

# with annotated colors
pHop_eff_E1891 = 
  tib_hop_eff_E1891 %>% 
  mutate(insert_name = factor(insert_name, levels = c("NanogS", "NanogL"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = insert_name, y = mean_fract_hopped, fill = insert_name)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "col", width = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = nanog_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = nanog_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  ggtitle("Hopped fraction of NanogS vs NanogL") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

pHop_eff_E1891
```
**Conclusion:**
Two technical replicates of NanogS (pCM002) and NanogL (pCM003) from E1845. Mean transposed fraction for NanogS = 0.47 (47%) versus NanogL = 0.37 (37%).
